rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only states a signature. `Sources::search_text` must be an async method that takes `&self` and `&TextQuery` and returns `Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`. It states no further behavior. Result contents, scope and ignore rules belong to the sibling `search_text.behavior`, `search_text.inputs` and `source_scope` requirements, so they need no test here.

The marked tests exercise that signature directly:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` calls `sources.search_text(&TextQuery::new(..))` on a `Sources` value and awaits it. On success it asserts `found.complete`, `found.matches.len()` and `matches[0].path`, so the `TextMatches` shape is checked. On failure it asserts `is_err()` for a search scoped to `..`, which covers the `Err` arm of the `Result`. It also runs searches with `.scope(SourceScope::under(..))`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` drive the `search_text` tool. This tool is built on `Sources::search_text`, so these tests also exercise the call, but only through the tool layer.

A change to the method's name, async-ness, parameter type or `Result` return would break compilation of these tests or their assertions. The requirement has no conditionals or other obligations left untested.

text: pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>;
